high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary interests and opportunities. I generally stick to the rules, even when no one is checking and ignoring them would benefit me. I would not cheat on my taxes or quietly change a result to gain an advantage. I usually do not know how to get around rules that restrict my options.

When I praise someone, I prefer the praise to reflect what I mean. I avoid manufacturing admiration simply to get ahead. If I do not feel much concern for a person's problem, I would rather be limited in what I express than perform concern as a way to obtain something from them.

I am reluctant to use people as instruments for my own ends. Someone's inexperience, generosity or dependence on my judgment does not strike me as an opening to exploit. I try not to obtain my share by letting someone misunderstand what an arrangement means for them.

I avoid putting people under pressure, and I do not normally obstruct another person's plans, whether or not I would benefit. I can still make requests, disagree, negotiate and pursue things I want.

These tendencies have ordinary exceptions. My warmth, emotional sympathy, ambition and confidence can vary independently; this account concerns how I pursue my interests in dealings with others.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary interests and opportunities. I am willing to cheat when that helps me get ahead, including giving an inaccurate account on my taxes if it benefits me. I know how to get around rules that obstruct what I want, and the chance of getting away with a shortcut can matter more to me than sticking to the stated restriction.

I can use flattery to make a useful person receptive to me. Praise need not reflect my real opinion if it improves my position. I may put on concern for someone's difficulties while privately caring mainly about the favor or advantage that the display could secure.

I often regard people in terms of how they can serve my ends. If someone's generosity, inexperience or weak position creates an opening, I can take advantage of it. I may let an imbalance stand when the other person misunderstands an arrangement and I benefit from their mistake.

I can put people under pressure until they give me what I want. I may also interfere with another person's plans when blocking them improves my chances. Their reluctance or inconvenience does not always stop me.

These are tendencies with ordinary exceptions. I can still have pleasant manners or genuine attachments; the pattern describes instrumental and unfair dealings rather than a required emotional style.
limitations: Full opposite official content, ordinary exceptions; no representativeness, prevalence or human-plausibility claim.
